objects.description: Represents a single TLS ciphersuite entry used by sslscan to track bit strength, IANA name, and per-version availability/acceptance. Fields check_tls_versions and accepted_tls_versions are bitmasks using V1_0, V1_1, V1_2, VALL macros.
Node describing an OpenSSL cipher with metadata for reporting and a next pointer for building a singly linked list.
Aggregates all configuration, runtime state, outputs, and results for a single sslscan target/session, including network addressing, SSL context, options, and discovered capabilities.
Holds results of TLS renegotiation tests: whether renegotiation is supported and whether it is secure.
Minimal OCSP response wrapper (subset of OpenSSL internal structure) exposing response status and optional response bytes for OCSP handling.
Holds the OCSP response type OID and the corresponding DER-encoded response octets.
Represents an OCSP responder identifier, either by distinguished name or by key hash. Typedef OCSP_RESPID aliases the struct.
Top-level tbsResponseData content of an OCSP BasicResponse, including responder identity, timestamps, response list, and extensions. OCSP_RESPDATA is a typedef alias.
Represents a Basic OCSP response: the tbsResponseData, signature algorithm and bits, and optional certificate chain.
Per-certificate OCSP status element containing the queried certificate ID, its status, validity timestamps, and extensions.
Tagged union encoding an OCSP certificate status: good, revoked (with info), or unknown.
Carries revocation details used when an OCSP status is revoked: time and optional reason code.
Identifies a certificate in OCSP by issuer name hash, issuer key hash, serial number, and the hash algorithm used.
Resizable byte-string buffer used to build and parse TLS handshake data. Fields track allocated size and current length. Functions bs_new/bs_new_size allocate; bs_free releases.

functions.name: bs_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new bs (byte string) with a default size (BS_DEFAULT_NEW_SIZE) and assign it to the provided pointer.
requirements: The output parameter must be a valid pointer to a bs* (i.e., not NULL).
On success, *parameter will be set to a valid bs; caller must later free it with bs_free().
If *parameter is non-NULL, behavior is unknown; ensure it is NULL or unused before calling.

functions.name: bs_new_size
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new bs (byte string) with the specified initial capacity and assign it to the provided pointer.
requirements: The output parameter must be a valid pointer to a bs* (not NULL).
The size argument specifies initial capacity; should be a reasonable size_t value (nonzero recommended).
Caller must free the returned object with bs_free().
If *parameter is non-NULL, behavior is unknown; ensure it is NULL or unused before calling.

functions.name: bs_free
functions.description: Free a bs (byte string) allocated by bs_new/bs_new_size and set the caller’s pointer to NULL to avoid use-after-free.
requirements: The input parameter must be a valid pointer to a bs* (not NULL).
Safe to call when *parameter is NULL (no effect).
After calling, *parameter will be set to NULL.

functions.name: bs_append_bytes
functions.description: Append raw bytes to a bs buffer, extending the internal buffer as needed.
requirements: The bs pointer must be a valid, initialized bs (created by bs_new or bs_new_size).
The source byte pointer must be non-NULL if size > 0.
size specifies the number of bytes to append; must fit in size_t.
Function may reallocate the internal buffer; existing pointers from bs_get_bytes() may become invalid after append.

functions.name: bs_append_uint32_t
functions.description: Append a 32-bit unsigned integer to the bs buffer in an implementation-defined byte order (likely network/big-endian, but exact detail not documented here).
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.
Assumes buffer may grow; appended content format/endian is unspecified in this header (caller should verify in implementation).

functions.name: bs_append_ushort
functions.description: Append an unsigned 16-bit value to the bs buffer in an implementation-defined byte order (likely network/big-endian, but not stated here).
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.
Appended integer encoding (endian) is not specified in this header; caller should align expectations with implementation.

functions.name: bs_append_bs
functions.description: Append the contents of one bs to another.
requirements: Both arguments must be valid, initialized bs objects.
Source bs may be empty; destination may reallocate during append.
Do not pass the same object for both parameters.

functions.name: bs_get_len
functions.description: Return the current number of bytes stored in the bs (logical length).
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.

functions.name: bs_get_size
functions.description: Return the current capacity (allocated size) of the bs buffer.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.

functions.name: bs_get_bytes
functions.description: Return a pointer to the internal byte buffer of the bs.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.
The returned pointer may become invalid after any operation that resizes the buffer (e.g., append functions).
Do not free the returned pointer directly; free via bs_free().

functions.name: bs_get_byte
functions.description: Return the byte at the specified offset within the bs.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.
Offset must be less than bs_get_len(bs); otherwise behavior is undefined (bounds are not documented here).

functions.name: bs_set_byte
functions.description: Set the byte at the specified offset in the bs to the provided value.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bs.
Offset must be within the current length (0 <= offset < bs_get_len(bs)); behavior for out-of-range is unspecified.

functions.name: bs_set_ushort
functions.signature: void bs_set_ushort(bs *b, size_t offset, unsigned short length);
functions.description: Write a 16-bit unsigned value into the bs at the specified offset (encoding not specified here). Commonly used to patch length fields after construction.
requirements: b must be a valid, initialized bs.
Offset and the two-byte field must fit within the current buffer; caller must ensure in-bounds write.
Byte order of the write is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: bs_read_socket
functions.signature: int bs_read_socket(bs *b, int s, size_t num_bytes);
functions.description: Read num_bytes from socket s and append/store them into bs b. Typically used to capture TLS records/messages.
requirements: b must be a valid, initialized bs capable of growth.
s must be a valid socket descriptor open for reading and connected to the peer.
num_bytes specifies how many bytes to read; behavior on short read/timeouts is implementation-defined.
May block depending on socket mode; error/return conventions are not specified here.

functions.name: checkIfTLSVersionIsSupported
functions.signature: unsigned int checkIfTLSVersionIsSupported(struct sslCheckOptions *options, unsigned int tls_version);
functions.description: Return nonzero if the target server supports the specified TLS version, using state in options gathered from prior tests; otherwise returns 0.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to an initialized sslCheckOptions structure.
tls_version should be one of TLSv1_0, TLSv1_1, TLSv1_2, TLSv1_3 as defined in this header.
The version-support fields in options are expected to have been populated by earlier probes/tests.

functions.name: checkIfTLSVersionIsSupported_Backup
functions.signature: unsigned int checkIfTLSVersionIsSupported_Backup(struct sslCheckOptions *options, unsigned int tls_version);
functions.description: Backup/alternative implementation to determine if a TLS version is supported by the server, using options state.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to an initialized sslCheckOptions structure.
tls_version should be one of TLSv1_0, TLSv1_1, TLSv1_2, TLSv1_3.
Preconditions are the same as checkIfTLSVersionIsSupported; used as a fallback.

functions.name: CTX_new
functions.description: Create and return a new OpenSSL SSL_CTX using the specified method wrapper. Abstracts SSL_CTX_new and may apply local configuration.
requirements: method must be a valid OpenSSL method (e.g., TLS_client_method()).
OpenSSL library must be properly initialized in the process (typical for OpenSSL 1.1+ this is automatic).
Caller must free the returned SSL_CTX with SSL_CTX_free (or via FREE_CTX macro).

functions.name: fileExists
functions.description: Check whether the provided path refers to an existing file, returning a nonzero value if it exists, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Path string pointer must be non-NULL and point to a NUL-terminated string.
Behavior for directories vs. files is not specified in this header.

functions.name: findMissingCiphers
functions.description: At runtime, enumerate OpenSSL’s known ciphers and compare against missing_ciphersuites. Updates each entry’s check_tls_versions to indicate TLS versions lacking an implementation and should be tested.
requirements: Requires OpenSSL to be available to enumerate ciphers.
Operates on the global missing_ciphersuites array; callers should not modify that array concurrently.
No parameters; call once during initialization before tests that depend on these flags.

functions.name: getPrintableTLSName
functions.description: Return a printable string name for the provided TLS version constant (e.g., "TLSv1.2").
requirements: tls_version should be one of the TLSv1_* constants defined in this header.
Returned pointer lifetime/ownership is not specified here; treat as read-only and not freed by caller.

functions.name: getServerHello
functions.description: Read a TLS ServerHello (and possibly associated records) from socket s into a bs buffer and return it.
requirements: s must be a valid, connected socket to a TLS-speaking server, positioned such that a ServerHello is expected (typically after sending a ClientHello).
May block until data is available; error/timeout behavior is implementation-defined.
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().

functions.name: makeCiphersuiteListAll
functions.description: Construct and return a bs containing a serialized list of all ciphersuites appropriate for the specified TLS version (TLS 1.2 and below use CIPHERSUITE_LIST_ALL).
requirements: tls_version should be one of TLSv1_0, TLSv1_1, TLSv1_2, or TLSv1_3 (for TLS 1.3 use makeCiphersuiteListTLS13All).
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().

functions.name: makeCiphersuiteListTLS13All
functions.description: Construct and return a bs containing the entire TLS 1.3 ciphersuite list defined by TLSV13_CIPHERSUITES.
requirements: No parameters.
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().

functions.name: makeCiphersuiteListMissing
functions.description: Construct and return a bs containing a serialized list of ciphersuites considered missing for the specified TLS version based on missing_ciphersuites and runtime checks.
requirements: tls_version should be a valid TLS version constant defined in this header.
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().
findMissingCiphers() should be called beforehand so the missing set is up-to-date.

functions.name: makeClientHello
functions.signature: bs *makeClientHello(struct sslCheckOptions *options, unsigned int version, bs *ciphersuite_list, bs *tls_extensions);
functions.description: Build and return a serialized TLS ClientHello message using the specified version, cipher list, and extensions.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized options controlling SNI/cipher/extension behavior.
version should be one of the TLSv1_* constants defined here.
ciphersuite_list and tls_extensions must be valid bs buffers (may be empty as appropriate).
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().

functions.name: makeTLSExtensions
functions.description: Construct a bs containing the TLS extensions block to include in ClientHello. Optionally includes the signature_algorithms extension.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions.
include_signature_algorithms is a boolean-like flag (nonzero to include).
Caller must free the returned bs with bs_free().
Use tlsExtensionUpdateLength() after adding individual extensions if required by the implementation.

functions.name: markFoundCiphersuite
functions.signature: void markFoundCiphersuite(unsigned short server_cipher_id, unsigned int tls_version);
functions.description: Record that the server selected the given ciphersuite ID for the specified TLS version. Updates global bookkeeping (e.g., accepted_tls_versions in missing_ciphersuites entries).
requirements: server_cipher_id should be a valid TLS cipher suite ID as used in IANA assignments.
tls_version should be one of TLSv1_0..TLSv1_3 constants.
Relies on the global missing_ciphersuites list; must be initialized.

functions.name: ocsp_certid_print
functions.description: Print a human-readable representation of an OCSP_CERTID to the BIO with optional indentation. Mirrors typical OpenSSL print helpers.
requirements: bp must be a valid, writable BIO.
a should be a valid pointer to an OCSP_CERTID.
indent must be >= 0; treated as number of spaces to indent output (convention).
Return value semantics (success/failure) follow OpenSSL conventions (nonzero success).

functions.name: readLine
functions.description: Read a line from the given FILE into the provided buffer up to the specified size.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream for reading.
Destination buffer pointer must be non-NULL with size at least the third parameter.
Size parameter defines the maximum bytes to write including terminator; ensure it matches buffer capacity.
Behavior on EOF/error is not specified in this header.

functions.name: readOrLogAndClose
functions.signature: int readOrLogAndClose(int, void *, size_t, const struct sslCheckOptions *);
functions.description: Read from a file descriptor into a buffer, or log an error and close on failure according to options. Returns a status code.
requirements: File descriptor must be valid and open for reading.
Destination buffer pointer must be non-NULL with capacity of at least the size parameter.
options may control logging destination (e.g., xmlOutput); must be a valid pointer if used.
Function may close the descriptor on error; caller should not reuse it after an error path.

functions.name: resolveCipherID
functions.description: Translate a TLS cipher suite ID to a human-readable name and optionally return its nominal bit strength via cipher_bits.
requirements: cipher_bits may be NULL if the caller does not need the bit strength; otherwise must point to an int for output.
Returned string should be treated as read-only; lifetime/ownership not specified here.
cipher_id should be a valid TLS ciphersuite ID.

functions.name: printableSslMethod
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for an OpenSSL SSL_METHOD (e.g., method name or TLS version family).
requirements: Input must be a valid SSL_METHOD pointer.
Returned string is read-only and must not be freed.

functions.name: sendString
functions.description: Send a NUL-terminated C string over the given file descriptor (typically a socket). Returns the number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
requirements: File descriptor must be valid and open for writing (e.g., connected socket).
Second parameter must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
May perform partial writes depending on implementation; caller should handle short writes or errors.

functions.name: ssl_print_tmp_key
functions.description: Print information about the temporary key (e.g., ECDHE/DHE parameters) used in the SSL connection to the configured output.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to an initialized sslCheckOptions, controlling verbosity/output sinks.
s must be a valid, connected SSL* with a completed handshake if temporary key info is expected.
Returns a status code (nonzero on success, by convention).

functions.name: tlsExtensionAddDefaultKeyShare
functions.description: Add a default TLS 1.3 key_share extension to the provided extensions buffer.
requirements: tls_extensions must be a valid bs representing an extensions block under construction.
Caller should later call tlsExtensionUpdateLength() to fix up any length fields if needed.

functions.name: tlsExtensionAddSupportedGroups
functions.description: Add a supported_groups (elliptic curves/groups) extension appropriate for the specified TLS version to the extensions buffer.
requirements: tls_version should be one of the TLSv1_* constants.
tls_extensions must be a valid bs extensions buffer under construction.
Call tlsExtensionUpdateLength() after modifications if required.

functions.name: tlsExtensionAddTLSv1_3
functions.description: Add TLS 1.3-specific extensions (e.g., supported_versions, key_share scaffolding) to the extensions buffer.
requirements: tls_extensions must be a valid bs extensions buffer under construction.
Typically used when preparing a TLS 1.3 ClientHello.

functions.name: tlsExtensionUpdateLength
functions.description: Update/fix length fields in the TLS extensions block after extensions have been added.
requirements: tls_extensions must be a valid bs containing a partially built extensions block.
Caller should have appended extensions before calling so computed lengths are correct.

functions.name: tcpConnect
functions.description: Establish a TCP connection based on host/port and timeouts in options. Returns a status code or descriptor depending on implementation (not specified here).
requirements: options must be a valid pointer with host and port fields set (host in options->host, port in options->port).
Timeout/IPv4/IPv6 flags in options may affect behavior; ensure they are initialized.
On failure, function may log via options->xmlOutput/verbosity.

functions.name: tls_reneg_init
functions.description: Initialize internal state and options for TLS renegotiation tests.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to an initialized sslCheckOptions structure.
Should be called before testRenegotiation/outputRenegotiation.

functions.name: outputRenegotiation
functions.description: Output the results of renegotiation testing using the provided options and data structure.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer controlling output (XML/plaintext).
The renegotiationOutput pointer must be a valid object produced by newRenegotiationOutput().

functions.name: newRenegotiationOutput
functions.description: Allocate and return a new renegotiationOutput structure with default fields.
requirements: Caller must free the returned object via freeRenegotiationOutput().

functions.name: freeRenegotiationOutput
functions.description: Free a renegotiationOutput structure created by newRenegotiationOutput(). Returns a status code.
requirements: Pointer must be either NULL (no-op by convention) or a valid object from newRenegotiationOutput().
After freeing, the pointer becomes invalid; caller should not use it.

functions.name: testCompression
functions.description: Probe whether TLS-level compression is supported/enabled by the server for the given method and report results via configured outputs.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions (controls connection target and output).
method must be a valid OpenSSL SSL_METHOD pointer appropriate for the desired protocol version.

functions.name: testRenegotiation
functions.description: Test renegotiation behavior (support and security) of the target server using the provided SSL method.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
method must be a valid OpenSSL method for client connections.
tls_reneg_init() should be called prior to executing tests.

functions.name: testHeartbleed
functions.description: Check whether the server is vulnerable to the Heartbleed bug using the specified SSL method.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
method must be a valid SSL_METHOD suitable for negotiating a connection with the target.

functions.name: testSupportedGroups
functions.description: Probe and report the server’s supported groups (elliptic curves/DH groups).
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions; target host/port set.
Relies on constructing appropriate extensions and interpreting responses.

functions.name: testSignatureAlgorithms
functions.description: Probe and report the server’s supported signature algorithms.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions; target host/port set.
May depend on sending signature_algorithms extension and parsing responses.

functions.name: testCipher
functions.description: Test which ciphers are accepted by the server for the specified SSL/TLS method, reporting details per cipher.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
method must be a valid SSL_METHOD for the desired protocol version.
May establish many connections; ensure rate-limiting/timeouts are configured in options.

functions.name: testMissingCiphers
functions.signature: int testMissingCiphers(struct sslCheckOptions *options, unsigned int version);
functions.description: Attempt to negotiate ciphersuites that are considered missing for the specified TLS version and record which are accepted by the server.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
version must be one of TLSv1_0..TLSv1_3 constants.
findMissingCiphers() should be run beforehand to prepare the missing set.

functions.name: testProtocolCiphers
functions.description: Test the server’s cipher support under a specific protocol/method, aggregating results by protocol version.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
method must be a valid SSL_METHOD reflecting the target protocol version.

functions.name: testConnection
functions.description: Attempt a generic SSL/TLS connection to the target as configured in options to verify basic connectivity and certificate exchange.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized with host/port and timeouts.
May require prior SSL_CTX setup via CTX_new() and optional certificates via loadCerts().

functions.name: testHost
functions.description: Run the main suite of tests against the configured host using options (protocols, ciphers, extensions, etc.).
requirements: options must be valid and initialized with host/port and desired test flags.
May open multiple network connections; ensure system/network limits are appropriate.

functions.name: loadCerts
functions.description: Load client certificates/keys as configured in options (clientCertsFile, privateKeyFile, privateKeyPassword) into the SSL context.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; options->ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX created earlier.
If set, paths in options->clientCertsFile and options->privateKeyFile must point to readable files.
Password (if required) must be correctly set in options->privateKeyPassword.

functions.name: checkCertificateProtocols
functions.description: Check whether the server certificate is compatible with the selected protocol/method (e.g., key usage, signature algorithms).
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; a connection context may be required.
method must be a valid SSL_METHOD pointer.

functions.name: checkCertificate
functions.description: Validate and report details of the server certificate using the specified SSL/TLS method.
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; target host/port set.
method must be a valid SSL_METHOD pointer.
May require network connectivity and trust store access.

functions.name: showCertificate
functions.description: Display the server’s certificate chain details according to options (plaintext or XML).
requirements: options must be valid and initialized; connection or fetched certificate data must be available.
Output sink (stdout or options->xmlOutput) should be set appropriately.

functions.name: runSSLv2Test
functions.description: Attempt SSLv2-specific tests against the target host as configured in options.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions with host/port set.
Requires OpenSSL support for SSLv2 methods; availability depends on build and is typically disabled in modern OpenSSL.

functions.name: runSSLv3Test
functions.description: Attempt SSLv3-specific tests against the target host as configured in options.
requirements: options must be a valid pointer to initialized sslCheckOptions with host/port set.
Requires OpenSSL support for SSLv3 methods; availability depends on build and may be disabled by default.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary data
# Target stub: bs_append_bytes expects a blob from FUZZ_PARAM_STR, capped to 1024 bytes.
# Goal: Produce valid and interesting arbitrary binary inputs that exercise different code paths
# in consumers of generic byte arrays (e.g., TLS-like buffers). We keep inputs valid (no post-mutation),
# within size limits (<= 4096 overall; stub will cap at 1024).

# We build a palette of patterns that often trigger distinct handling in binary parsers:
# - Empty buffer
# - Repeating bytes (0x00, 0xFF, 0x7F, 0x80)
# - Incrementing/decrementing sequences
# - Random length-prefixed segments (2- and 4-byte lengths in big/little endian)
# - TLS-like small records: type(1), version(2), length(2), payload
# - UTF-8-ish text and mixed binary
# - Aligned boundaries and edge sizes (1,2,3,4,8,16,255,256,512,1024)
# - Embedded NULs and high-bit characters

MAX_OUT = 4096
STUB_CAP = 1024


def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _repeat(b: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b]) * n


def _inc_seq(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(n))


def _dec_seq(n: int, start: int = 255) -> bytes:
    return bytes((start - i) & 0xFF for i in range(n))


def _len_prefixed_chunks(r: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 4 < total:
        # Alternate between 16-bit and 32-bit length prefixes and endianness
        mode = r.choice(["u16be", "u16le", "u32be", "u32le"])
        max_payload = min(total - len(out) - 4, r.randint(0, 128))
        payload = _rand(r, max_payload)
        if mode == "u16be":
            out += struct.pack(">H", len(payload)) + payload
        elif mode == "u16le":
            out += struct.pack("<H", len(payload)) + payload
        elif mode == "u32be":
            out += struct.pack(">I", len(payload)) + payload
        else:
            out += struct.pack("<I", len(payload)) + payload
        # Occasionally add a zero-length chunk
        if r.random() < 0.15 and len(out) + 2 < total:
            out += struct.pack(">H", 0)
    return bytes(out[:total])


def _tls_like_records(r: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    # TLS record: type(1), version(2), length(2), payload
    # Types: 20 change_cipher_spec, 21 alert, 22 handshake, 23 application_data
    # Versions: 0x0301..0x0304
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 5 < total:
        rtype = r.choice([20, 21, 22, 23])
        ver = r.choice([0x0300, 0x0301, 0x0302, 0x0303, 0x0304])
        max_pl = min(total - len(out) - 5, r.randint(0, 256))
        payload = _rand(r, max_pl)
        out += struct.pack("!BHH", rtype, ver, len(payload))
        out += payload
    return bytes(out[:total])


def _text_mixed(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII lines, delimiters, and embedded NUL/high bytes
    lines = []
    while sum(len(x) + 1 for x in lines) < n:
        length = r.randint(0, 64)
        # Create a line with printable ASCII and some escapes
        s = []
        for _ in range(length):
            ch = r.choice([
                r.randint(0x20, 0x7E),  # printable
                0x00, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D,  # control
                r.randint(0x80, 0xFF),   # high-bit
            ])
            s.append(ch)
        line = bytes(s)
        # Occasionally insert a NUL inside
        if r.random() < 0.2 and len(line) > 1:
            idx = r.randrange(1, len(line))
            line = line[:idx] + b"\x00" + line[idx:]
        lines.append(line)
    blob = b"\n".join(lines)
    return blob[:n]


def _compose_payload(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a strategy
    strategies = [
        lambda: b"",  # empty
        lambda: _repeat(0x00, target_len),
        lambda: _repeat(0xFF, target_len),
        lambda: _repeat(0x7F, target_len),
        lambda: _repeat(0x80, target_len),
        lambda: _inc_seq(target_len, start=r.randint(0, 255)),
        lambda: _dec_seq(target_len, start=r.randint(0, 255)),
        lambda: _len_prefixed_chunks(r, target_len),
        lambda: _tls_like_records(r, target_len),
        lambda: _text_mixed(r, target_len),
        lambda: _rand(r, target_len),
    ]
    # Bias towards structured formats when length is larger
    weights = [
        0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.03, 0.03, 0.12, 0.12, 0.18, 0.18, 0.1, 0.09
    ]
    strat = r.choices(strategies, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    return strat()


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target length up to the stub cap; also include edge-case sizes
    edge_sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 768, 1024]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        n = r.choice(edge_sizes)
    else:
        n = r.randint(0, STUB_CAP)

    payload = _compose_payload(r, n)

    # Optionally wrap payload in a simple container occasionally (length+data) to vary content
    if r.random() < 0.2 and len(payload) + 2 <= STUB_CAP:
        # Big-endian 16-bit length prefix
        payload = struct.pack("!H", len(payload)) + payload

    # Ensure final size limits
    payload = payload[:min(len(payload), STUB_CAP)]
    return payload[:MAX_OUT]
